name: Operation Long Night
summary: Hypothetical scenario: the uprising reaches an invented capital. Protect the crowds in the central square, retake the broadcast house, win the guard barracks over and secure the ministries and archives intact for the civilian government to come.

states.objective: Briefing: the people of Gulshar are in the streets. The regime has little left but its hardliners. Protect the crowds and win the city without a siege.
Meet the resistance council at the assembly hall. Defectors from the capital guard arrive; accept them.
Choose the first front. Take the broadcast house to silence regime propaganda, or reach the guard barracks first and offer the guard a way out.
Retake the state broadcast house so the people and the guard hear the same message.
Offer the capital guard barracks the chance to surrender or defect.
Reach the capital guard barracks and offer the guard the chance to surrender or defect.
Hardline enforcers move on the central square. Shield the crowds and get the people to safe streets. The crowd is never a target.
Secure the ministries and public archives intact, with no looting. The records belong to the people.
Bring aid to the northern districts and the field hospitals.
Broadcast the final surrender offer. The remaining regime forces lay down arms, or withdraw to a last enclave.
Debrief: the capital, the archives, the crowds and the surrendered.
The capital is free, the archives are safe and the regime has surrendered. The interim assembly can meet.
The capital is free, but a hardliner remnant holds out and the city bears scars. The interim assembly will meet under threat.
The operation failed: the square was lost or too many civilians were harmed. Restart from the last checkpoint.
